# EngageLab Agent Email MCP Server

> Local stdio MCP server for EngageLab Agent Email: each AI agent gets its own mailbox — send, receive, monitor and reply to email with thread context, through the Model Context Protocol.

Install: `npx -y @engagelabemail/mcp` (npm package `@engagelabemail/mcp`, MIT, Node >= 20)
Config: `mcpServers` entry with command `npx`, args `["-y", "@engagelabemail/mcp"]`, env `ENGAGELAB_EMAIL_SECRET_KEY=sk_sg_your_key` (region inferred from key prefix `sk_sg_` / `sk_tr_`)
Works with: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, and any MCP-compatible client.

Tools (9):

- `list_mailboxes` — list mailboxes; call first to get IDs
- `send_email` — new email (text/html, cc/bcc, attachments, sandbox)
- `reply_email` — reply to a message; recipients & thread inferred (keeps threading headers intact)
- `list_inbound_messages` — inbound mail, filter by mailbox/keyword
- `get_message` — full message details by UID
- `check_new_messages` — one-shot poll for new mail
- `list_threads` / `get_thread` / `list_thread_messages` — browse conversations

Notes: up to 10 attachments / 10MB per message (base64 in tool schema); sandbox mode for testing without emailing real humans; agents cannot self-provision mailboxes yet — create one in the EngageLab console first.

Related tools:

- CLI `@engagelabemail/cli` (https://github.com/Metaverse-Cloud/engagelab-email-cli)
- Node SDK `engagelab-email` (https://github.com/Metaverse-Cloud/engagelab-email-node)

Registry: listed in the official MCP Registry as `io.github.Metaverse-Cloud/engagelab-email`
Docs: https://github.com/Metaverse-Cloud/engagelab-email-mcp#readme
